scope: Unified Rust queue/gathering/query/party registry and native advertisement/IO lifecycle. Existing original numerical fixtures are reused; authenticated original service/summary/QoS inputs, full original callers, API/results and native/delivery acceptance remain open.
rust_authorities: Session identities, admission membership, birth and growth clocks
Per-party state, lifecycle jitter and current search/view generations
Ordered query IDs, native birth/id provider and original50-record bank cap
Complete per-query candidate bank/cache and original selector calls
Native advertisement projection from admitted raw roster, selected rank map, age, clan, language and measured relay facts
Probe allocation/pending/failure/seen transitions and completion-driven radius/exhaustion
Query selection, group joining, founding game preservation and proposal publication
Cancellation, expiry and profile-change retirement of registries, views and IO continuations
Pure progress projection without RNG, query allocation or peak mutation

io_boundary.continuations: Private monotonically generated tokens bind requested readiness/measurement/allocation results to Rust work. Count/type-invalid replies are rejected before taking the continuation; stale/replayed replies and aborts cannot target new work.
io_boundary.adapter: Python executes only Rust-requested existing authenticated QoS calls; it holds immutable projections, not registry/cache/seen/matching policy.
io_boundary.retirement: Queue cancellation and same-revision profile changes immediately retire actual Rust state. Saved views do not keep an independent live lifecycle owner.
io_boundary.atomicity_limit: Individual private commands are serialized. The existing service pumps multi-command IO synchronously on one event loop. This is not distributed transaction or exactly-once network allocation proof.

modern_replacements: Birth/private-ID service ordering and synchronous50-record native queries
Relay-route three-sample median and unknown quality0/-1 projection
Native structural membership/capacity and12-second allocation-refusal wait
Private IO generations and stale-view safeguards
